name: teenage-engineering
title: Teenage Engineering
description: Tactile industrial product UI with technical labels, physical grid borders, utilitarian surfaces, and high-visibility international orange.

typography.monospaceFamily: IBM Plex Mono, SFMono-Regular, Consolas, monospace

rules: Treat controls as physical instrument panels with explicit labels, alignment, and tactile feedback.
Use international orange for active controls and critical landmarks only.
Technical monospace labels are uppercase, tracked, concise, and paired with readable body text.
Expose the eight-column hardware grid through one-pixel rules and exact registration.
Use small offset hard shadows for pressable mechanical elements, not ambient decoration.
Keep radio, LED, and status colors semantically consistent and labelled.
Every pointer action needs a keyboard equivalent and a visible focus state.
Use tabular readouts for frequency, time, battery, levels, and numerical parameters.
Do not soften the system with glass, glow, gradient, or oversized bubble radii.
Feedback is immediate—100ms—and reduced-motion mode removes travel rather than meaning.
